industry.why: Overweight, carried unchanged. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): Brent $111 (Jefferies, 22 Oct), oil above $100 and rising, and energy led the week; energy is the hedge inside a European book against the shock that hurts everything else. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior at industry level. Not Double Overweight at the industry because the industry holds Metals and mining (relative strength F now from A) and Agriculture beside the three energy sectors; Downstream distribution carries the A. Counter-case: Goldman attributes part of the oil move to restocking, two months into leadership is where reversals begin, and 13 of the 18 upstream Pool names read F on TSR/Valuation, so the market has paid.

sector.why: Overweight, carried. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): Brent near $115 and oil the inflation risk Goldman Sachs worries about most, with Iran the two-sided swing; Equinor solid with a lifted production guide and a balance sheet that pressures it to raise buybacks (Danske Bank, 28 October); against it, Nordic exploration and production names lagged as crude eased on de-escalation (DNB Carnegie, 26 October) and Rosebank was written into the UK's fiscal arithmetic. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: A now, A prior, agrees. Eighteen Pool names, the largest sector in the Pool, with 15 energy names in the top 40 of the starting score, which is why the sector cap on the Lists (component 5, amendment 6) stays. Counter-case: producers move with crude and crude eased late in the week. Back to C if Brent falls under $85.

geography.why: Neutral, carried as a judgement with the evidence now read both ways, on the special topic 'The UK Budget of 28-Oct-26': the Budget removed a UK-specific fiscal tail risk from the discount rate without lowering it (headroom £15bn, both rules met, the 10-year gilt about 5.32% and its lowest in over a month, gilts outperforming Bunds and Treasuries by about 5 basis points), and the UK data beat on every count (growth 0.7% on three months, employment up 102,000, purchasing managers' indices beating; Pacific, 26 October); against it, 2027 growth cut to 1.0% from 1.6%, unemployment 5.1% in 2027, the energy price cap up about 16% in January, a Bank of England rise to 4.00% almost priced for 5-Nov-26, and banks made the first payer in the next shock. Neutral against Underweight was tested; the data say the consumer slows rather than breaks, so Neutral, with no weight carried in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44). 22 of the 144 Pool stocks are UK-listed. Counter-case: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance on 5-Nov-26, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.

memo.verdict: PARK. Medium-high conviction. Direction neutral with a bearish tilt on the entry point, not bearish on the business. The memo places BP-GB on the watchlist at long-list qualified with an automatic reassessment at the Q3 2026 print (expected November 2026) and a second at the Q4 2026 print (expected February 2027). The park is conditional and expires on evidence rather than on a calendar. Three numeric release triggers, all of which must clear before progression to Early-Stage Assessment is recommended: (1) net debt excluding leases inside USD 14-18bn at end-2026 with buyback reinstatement parameters formally announced; (2) the refining indicator margin sustaining above USD 15/bbl through Q3 and Q4 2026, measured against BP's own USD 10.80/bbl normalised planning baseline; (3) upstream plant reliability recovering above 95% for two consecutive quarters from 92.4% in Q2 2026, with refining availability back above the stated 96% standard. Two kill triggers: Brent below USD 65/bbl for two consecutive quarters with the refining indicator margin below USD 10/bbl; or full-year 2026 divestment proceeds guided below USD 12bn against the USD 15-16bn management now guides by end-2026.
case: The Triaging stage test asks whether the case has large amounts of positive change forces. BP passes that test emphatically, and the memo grades Element E1 [B] on it. The change is not narrative: every component is a dated fact with a source. A chief executive appointed 1 April 2026. A segment structure changed effective 1 July 2026. A disposal process launched 31 July 2026. A debt target moved on 4 August 2026. The memo's judgement is that this is the largest corporate-change agenda in the six-peer set.

The internal change is the strongest single feature of the case. Meg O'Neill is the first external chief executive in BP's 116-year history and an operating engineer rather than a financier, which Bernstein Research reads as reinforcing a back-to-basics capital allocation strategy. The three-to-two segment collapse removes the structure Bernard Looney set in 2020. Transition growth capital has been cut 75% to below USD 0.80bn a year and the 50 GW renewables target has been formally retired, which is a complete inversion of the prior decade's direction. Elliott Management's 5% stake operates as an external enforcement mechanism on capital discipline.

The balance-sheet change is the most measurable. Net debt excluding leases fell USD 3,058m in a single quarter to USD 22,251m, below consensus. Total financial obligations fell to USD 53.6bn from USD 60.5bn at Q1 2026 and are guided to USD 39-41bn by end-2026. EUR 2.5bn of perpetual hybrids were redeemed in Q2 with a further USD 1.0bn scheduled for Q3, targeting a USD 9.0bn stack. Most importantly, management pulled the primary USD 14-18bn net debt target forward a full year to end-2026. Redburn projects net debt excluding leases falling to USD 10.0bn on Castrol close, which would clear the target without further commodity help.
counter_case: The counter-case is that all of the above is a price event wearing the clothes of an operating event, and the memo grades it [F] on Element E8 RA8. This is the memo's load-bearing finding and it must not be softened.

Five false friends are named in the Risks report and all five are simultaneously present in the Q2 2026 print. First, transient refining margin spikes: the refining indicator margin averaged USD 29.60/bbl, nearly three times BP's own USD 10.80/bbl normalised planning baseline, and up from USD 11.90/bbl a year earlier. Second, temporary working capital releases: management guides USD 2.0-3.0bn of working capital to unwind in the second half after a USD 7,046m first-half build. Third, publicised cost-outs that do not reach earnings: Meg O'Neill conceded that structural cost cuts have not yet translated into bottom-line improvement, with about USD 3bn absorbed by inflation and activity choices. Fourth, accelerated disposal announcements masking portfolio value destruction: net debt is falling partly on Castrol, Gelsenkirchen and North Sea proceeds while proved reserve life stays at 7.1 years and three-year organic reserve replacement at 39%. Fifth, exceptional trading earnings: trading has historically contributed up to one third of group earnings in volatile quarters, and Q2 2026 was exceptionally volatile.
triggers: Release triggers, all three required. Net debt excluding leases inside USD 14-18bn at end-2026 with buyback reinstatement parameters formally announced. The refining indicator margin sustaining above USD 15/bbl through Q3 and Q4 2026, measured against BP's own USD 10.80/bbl normalised baseline. Upstream plant reliability recovering above 95% for two consecutive quarters from 92.4%, with refining availability back above the stated 96% standard.

Kill triggers. Brent below USD 65/bbl for two consecutive quarters with the refining indicator margin below USD 10/bbl, which the Earnings Review report names as the signal that targets need asset fire-sales. Full-year 2026 divestment proceeds guided below USD 12bn against the USD 15-16bn now guided.

What would flip the verdict to progress. A Q3 2026 print showing net debt inside target with the refining indicator margin already back near USD 15/bbl would clear the false-friend objection outright. What would make it a permanent exit: a failed Bumerangue appraisal alongside Brent below USD 65/bbl, leaving neither a resource story nor a cash story.

Open questions carried to Early-Stage Assessment. Does the Q4 2026 print show net debt inside target with the refining margin already normalised, or only with it still elevated? Element E9 (Great operator) and Element E10 (Advantaged business and widening competitive advantage) must both be built, since the Deep Dive mediocrity gate parks [C] or worse on business quality. Element E3 (Sufficient total-shareholder-return / valuation upside) must clear a 25% internal-rate-of-return hurdle from a price already up 28.2% in twelve months. Reconcile the 7.1-year proved reserve life against the 23-year resource life claim, and establish whether Bumerangue changes the reserve replacement trajectory. Establish how much of the USD 22bn to USD 18bn cost path reaches the bottom line given about USD 3bn already absorbed. Quantify what the UK North Sea, Archaea and Castrol exits remove from group cash generation, not just what they add to the disposal total.

Element E8 carve-out for Early-Stage Assessment. Primary fit setup: RA3, strong corporate change driven earnings-per-share upgrade or earnings-power turn, at [B], to be deepened first, focusing on whether the disposal programme converts from announced to completed at guided prices. Secondary: RA4, change-from-current clearing in a high-quality compounder, at [C], carried conditionally and to be deepened only if Element E9 and Element E10 grade [B] or better. RA1, RA2, RA5 and RA6 all grade [D] and carry forward at the light three-bullet floor without deepening.

Monitoring instructions. Run the five false friends as a standing quarterly checklist from the Q3 2026 print, since this is the reading that decides the case. Re-count the change-from-current items after the Q4 2026 print, since three of the eight should have closed. Track the Kaskida litigation docket quarterly, since an adverse ruling removes an 80,000 barrel a day project from the volume plan. Commission a refreshed Change Forces family report after the Q4 2026 print, since the current one carries Q1 2026 data. Commission the outstanding Q3 2026 thematics review and an AlphaSense cross-check on Thematic 4.
